record.paper_title: Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology
record.original_question: A compact space X is ω-monolithic if the closure of every countable subset of X is metrizable. Must every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact space be first-countable?

evidence.quote:
A compact space X is
ω-monolithic if the closure of any countable subset of X is metrizable.

Problem 15 (Arhangel’skii, 1987) . Is every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact
space X ﬁrst-countable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological space is called compact if it is Hausdorff and every open cover has a finite subcover. A space X is said to be ω-monolithic if for every countable subset A ⊆ X, the closure A̅ is metrizable. A space X is homogeneous if for every pair of points x, y ∈ X, there is a homeomorphism h: X → X with h(x) = y. A space X is first-countable if every point has a countable neighborhood base.

Question: Must every homogeneous, ω-monolithic compact space be first-countable?
artifact.status_search_result: The question, attributed to Arhangelskii (1987), appears in compilations of long-standing open problems in general topology and is discussed in surveys on topological homogeneity by Arhangelskii and van Mill. No published resolution was located; the problem appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: Topological Homogeneity — Arhangel'skii and van Mill
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on topological homogeneity covering open questions about homogeneous compact spaces, monolithicity, and first-countability.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is discussed in this survey alongside other open questions on homogeneous compacta without a stated solution.
